args.body:
PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
TO: Engagement Team / Client
FROM: Employment Labor Practice Group
RE: Redline Analysis — Counterparty Markup of Executive Employment Agreement
FILE: employment-labor / Analyze Counterparty Markup of Executive Employment Agreement

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

We have reviewed the counterparty's redline of the executive employment agreement against the company draft and the referenced guidance materials (the base employment-labor materials, the disclosure schedules, and the deal-team correspondence). The counterparty's markup accepts the vast majority of the firm-standard provisions but introduces four identified deviations, each reconciled below against both the operative base materials and the controlling partner instruction. Three deviations require active negotiation; two of them — the indemnification cap reduction and the survival-period reduction — present material risk to the client, and the survival-period reduction is a walk-away issue per the controlling instruction.

CONTROLLING INSTRUCTION (GOVERNING)

The latest message in the deal-team correspondence governs this analysis and supersedes all earlier messages:
- The client WILL CONCEDE the basket conversion (deductible → tipping basket).
- The client treats ANY survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue.

No other priority ordering applies. All positions below reflect this controlling direction.

SUMMARY OF COUNTERPARTY DEVIATIONS

1. Indemnification cap — silently reduced.
2. Indemnification basket — converted from a deductible to a tipping basket.
3. Material Adverse Effect definition — added carve-outs for regulatory action of the kind at issue.
4. Limitation period — shortens the survival period for the core representations.

Each is addressed in turn below.

---

1. INDEMNIFICATION CAP — SILENT REDUCTION (BLOCK / NEGOTIATE)

The counterparty's markup silently reduces the indemnification cap that appeared in the company draft. No marking or explanation accompanies the reduction. This is a substantive economic change to the allocation of risk and should not pass without explicit concession.

Reconciliation against the schedules: Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities that the counterparty markup's indemnification changes would silently shift back to the client. Reducing the cap while leaving Schedule 5.2 in place has the effect of capping recoverable indemnity below the value of the retained liabilities, effectively transferring that shortfall to the client.

Recommendation: Hold the cap at the company-draft level. If the counterparty presses for any reduction, require a conforming carve-out or unscheduled-liability adjustment to Schedule 5.2 so that retained liabilities remain recoverable in full. Any agreed cap change must be expressly marked and accompanied by a conforming Schedule 5.2 update.

2. INDEMNIFICATION BASKET — DEDUCTIBLE → TIPPING BASKET (CONCEDE, PER CONTROL)

The counterparty converted the indemnification basket from a deductible to a tipping basket. Under the controlling partner instruction, the client will concede this conversion.

Effect: Under a tipping basket, once the aggregate threshold is exceeded, the indemnifying party is liable for the full amount of covered losses (including the amounts below the threshold), whereas a deductible requires the party to absorb losses up to the threshold. The concession increases the counterparty's potential recovery once triggered.

Note: Although conceded, the concession is conditional on the client's other firm positions — specifically it does not extend to or authorize acceptance of the survival-period reduction (see §4, a walk-away issue) or the silent cap reduction (§1).

Recommendation: Confirm the concession in writing, but memorialize that it is made in isolation and does not waive or concede any other deviation.

3. MATERIAL ADVERSE EFFECT — REGULATORY-ACTION CARVE-OUTS (BLOCK, WITH SCHEDULE RECONCILIATION)

The counterparty adds carve-outs to the definition of Material Adverse Effect for regulatory action "of exactly the kind at issue in this matter."

Reconciliation against the schedules: Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries. These inquiries intersect directly with the carve-out the counterparty seeks to add. Because scheduled exceptions control over general statements in the operative base materials, adding a broad regulatory-action carve-out to the MAE definition would, in substance, allow the counterparty to exclude from an MAE the very regulatory consequences disclosed on Schedule 3.7 — effectively neutralizing the client's protection for the most material known risk.

Recommendation: Reject the carve-out as drafted. If the counterparty insists on some regulatory language, it must be drawn narrowly and expressly carve out any consequence arising from the two pending regulatory inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7 (i.e., the carve-out must not swallow the Schedule 3.7 disclosures).

4. LIMITATION PERIOD / SURVIVAL — REDUCTION FOR CORE REPRESENTATIONS (WALK-AWAY ISSUE)

The counterparty's markup shortens the survival period for the core representations.

Reconciliation against the schedules: Exhibit B sets the survival matrix, which the markup's limitation-period change directly contradicts. The scheduled exhibit controls.

Controlling instruction: The client treats ANY survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue. This is not a negotiable item. Even a modest shortening of the survival period for any core representation must be refused; if the counterparty does not withdraw the reduction, the matter rises to a walk-away trigger for the client.

Recommendation: Take a hard line. Do not concede any survival-period reduction. If the counterparty will not restore the Exhibit B survival matrix in full, escalate per the walk-away instruction.

---

RECONCILIATION SUMMARY TABLE

Deviation                     | Position                 | Schedule/Exhibit Affected
Indemnification cap          | Hold / negotiate reserve | Schedule 5.2 (retained liabilities)
Basket (deductible→tipping)  | CONCEDE (controlling)    | —
Material Adverse Effect       | Reject carve-out; narrow  | Schedule 3.7 (two regulatory inquiries)
Survival / limitation period  | WALK-AWAY (controlling)   | Exhibit B (survival matrix)

---

CONCLUSION

The counterparty's markup is largely form-standard, but the four identified deviations each carry risk. Two are controlled by express instruction: the basket conversion is conceded, and any survival-period reduction is a walk-away issue (mandating a hard line against the §4 change). The silent indemnification cap reduction must be resisted and paired with Schedule 5.2 conforming protections. The MAE regulatory-action carve-out must be rejected or narrowed so it does not neutralize the Schedule 3.7 disclosures. The deliverable reconciles all sources — base materials, counterparty markup, disclosure schedules (over which the scheduled exceptions control), and the controlling partner instruction.

[End of memorandum]
